arxiv-2406-00607.title: Smooth orbit equivalence rigidity for dissipative geodesic flows
arxiv-2406-00607.creator: Javier Echevarría Cuesta
arxiv-2406-00607.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Javier Echevarría Cuesta. Let M M be a smooth closed oriented surface. Gaussian thermostats on M M correspond to the geodesic flows arising from metric connections, including those with non-zero torsion. These flows may not preserve any absolutely continuous measure. We prove that if two Gaussian thermostats on M M with negative thermostat curvature are related by a smooth orbit equivalence isotopic to the identity, then the two background metrics are conformally equivalent via a smooth diffeomorphism of M M isotopic to the identity.

arxiv-2502-00329.title: CoddLLM : Empowering Large Language Models for Data Analytics Thanks: *Work done at AWS

arxiv-2502-00329.description: Abstract . Large Language Models (LLMs) have the potential to revolutionize data analytics by simplifying tasks such as data discovery and SQL query synthesis through natural language interactions. This work serves as a pivotal first step toward the development of foundation models explicitly designed for data analytics applications.

arxiv-2503-19627.title: femtoPro: Real-time linear and nonlinear optics simulations
arxiv-2503-19627.creator: Tobias Brixner, 1,* Stefan Mueller, 1 Andreas Müller, 2 and Sebastian von Mammen 2
arxiv-2503-19627.description: Abstract Real-time optics and spectroscopy simulations ideally provide results at update rates of 120 Hz or more without any noticeable delay between changing input parameters and the calculated results. Such calculations require models of sufficient speed yet adequate level of detail in the physical approximations to contain the essential features of the simulated phenomena.

arxiv-2504-18443.title: Pseudo-Boolean Proof Logging for Optimal Classical Planning
arxiv-2504-18443.creator: Simon Dold, Malte Helmert, Jakob Nordström, Gabriele Röger, Tanja Schindler
arxiv-2504-18443.description: Abstract We introduce lower-bound certificates for classical planning tasks, which can be used to prove the unsolvability of a task or the optimality of a plan in a way that can be verified by an independent third party. We describe a general framework for generating lower-bound certificates based on pseudo-Boolean constraints, which is agnostic to the planning algorithm used.

pmc-11621690.title: First evidence of early neolithic archery from Cueva de los Murciélagos (Albuñol, Granada) revealed through combined chemical and morphological analysis
pmc-11621690.creator: Ingrid Bertin, María Martín-Seijo, Francisco Martínez-Sevilla, Krista McGrath, Jonathan Santana, Maria Herrero-Otal, Rafael M Martínez Sánchez, Antoni Palomo, Martine Regert, Isabelle Théry, Raquel Piqué
pmc-11621690.description: The extraordinary preservation of Cueva de Los Murciélagos (Albuñol, Spain) provides a unique opportunity to identify the materials and the techniques involved in archery during the Early Neolithic period. pmc-12470132.title: In Vivo Immune Cell Responses and Long-Term Effects of Cold Atmospheric Plasma in the Upper Respiratory Tract
pmc-12470132.creator: Stephanie Arndt, Petra Unger, Lisa Gebhardt, Robert Schober, Mark Berneburg, Sigrid Karrer
pmc-12470132.description: Cold atmospheric plasma (CAP) devices produce reactive oxygen and reactive nitrogen species, which have antimicrobial and antiviral effects, while also affecting the molecular and cellular processes in eukaryotic cells. This study investigates the effects of CAP treatment on immune responses and long-term organism health in the upper respiratory tract (URT).

pmc-12654143.description: Background: Multiple primary malignant tumors (MPMTs) involving the digestive tract pose diagnostic and therapeutic challenges, with survival differences between synchronous and metachronous forms not well defined. This study assessed predictors of overall survival (OS) in patients in whom at least one tumor originated in the digestive tract or accessory organs.

pmc-12773396.title: Abstract 096: Hypoperfusion Intensity Ratio Suggests Collateral Status, Stroke Mechanism, and Clinical Stability in Large Vessel Occlusion
pmc-12773396.creator: Chris Gasparis, Justin Turpin, Christian Ferreira, David Langer, Ahmad Ballout
pmc-12773396.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). IntroductionHypoperfusion Intensity Ratio (HIR), defined by the ratio of Tmax >10s/Tmax >6s on perfusion imaging, has been directly correlated with collateral status, stroke mechanism, and clinical outcomes in patients with acute large vessel occlusions [1,2]. We report a case of a patient with mild neurological symptoms despite an acute MCA M1 occlusion in which a very favorable HIR may have predicted clinical stability, extensive atherosclerotic burden, and compensatory leptomeningeal collaterals.
